messages:
maya: quick check — we need p95=200ms / p99=800ms SLO math for EU-W1 for next quarter. seasonal spike forecast +35% peak, and networking flaps in the region last month. current fleet = 120 A100 GPUs (reserved 100, on-demand 20). avg service time per request at 8k tokens = 48ms (measured). current observed p99 ~1.1s during bursts. can we project required GPUs and propose admission thresholds?
dan: ok. start with basic queueing capacity approximation. If we treat each GPU as a worker with service time S = 48ms = 0.048s, then max throughput per GPU (1/S) = ~20.8 req/s. For p99 tail, use an M/M/c style approximation and conservative safety factor. load = req/s. We need to estimate peak req/s from token throughput — what's peak requests/sec now?
maya: peak baseline right now ~1,600 req/s across EU fleet during weekdays, bursts hit ~2,300 req/s. With +35% seasonal, burst ~3,105 req/s.
dan: math: required GPUs = peak_req_s / per_gpu_throughput. Using 3,105 / 20.8 = ~149 GPUs. That's just to keep utilization ~100% which kills latency. For p99 headroom we want target utilization u_target ~0.6-0.7 to avoid queueing tail. Using u_target=0.65 -> effective per-gpu throughput = 20.8 * 0.65 = 13.52 req/s. GPUs_needed = 3105 / 13.52 ≈ 230 GPUs.

Quick calc block:
```
S = 0.048s
mu = 1/S = 20.83 req/s
peak = 3105 req/s (35% seasonal burst)
util_target = 0.65
per_gpu_eff = mu * util_target = 13.54 req/s
GPUs_needed = ceil(peak / per_gpu_eff) = 230
```

dan: cost note: on-demand A100 ~ $3.10/hr (eu region) vs reserved commit ~ $1.95/hr. If we add 110 GPUs on-demand for peak months that's ~110 * 3.10 * 24 = $8,184/day. Consider mixing reserved + autoscale + soft-admit.
alex: that 230 number feels high but matches observed p99 degradation. We can tighten by reducing S via batching/quantization for certain routes. Example: reduce S to 36ms via int8 -> mu=27.78 -> per_gpu_eff @0.65 = 18.06 -> GPUs_needed = 3105/18.06 ≈ 172. Big savings.
serena: network flaps last month amplified queueing because cross-AZ retries doubled apparent S for some requests. If we provision more GPUs but keep same AZ spread, we also need to harden network (NLB health checks, increase LB timeout). Otherwise extra capacity won't net lower p99.
oncall-bot: NOTE: eu-west-1 experienced 3 transient packet drops on 2026-02-12 03:14 UTC; see incident 2026-02-12-147.
cost-ops: ops question — do we have budget for an additional 50 reserved GPUs? committed pricing negotiation possible if we commit 12-18 months. Also suggest using spot for 30% of burst capacity where jobs tolerate preemption.

maya: proposed admission control policy:
- soft-admit at 70% of capacity (signal warn, allow but use degraded model variant)
- hard-admit at 85% (reject with 429 + small cached summary)
- per-GPU concurrent request cap = 40 (empirically stable)
- route-level priority: interactive chat > batch embed > long-llm-rerank

Config snippet suggestion:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_gpus: 120
  target_utilization: 0.65
  max_gpus: 260
admission_control:
  soft_threshold: 0.70
  hard_threshold: 0.85
  per_gpu_concurrency_limit: 40
  fallback_model: gptq-7b-degraded
```

alex: simulation note — run a short-run stochastic sim (10k runs) that includes network-induced S spikes (x2 for 5% of requests) and quantization effect. We should produce p95/p99 distributions and show what fraction of time we violate.
serena: action items: 1) run sim (alex) 2) trial int8 on a subset of traffic (alex/maya) 3) talk to procurement about 50 GPU reserve (maya + cost-ops) 4) implement soft/hard admit in routing (eng-platform)
maya: thanks. I'll kick off the simulation and draft a short cost vs latency tradeoff doc. if results look like 172 GPUs after int8, we prioritise quantization + 60 reserved GPUs + 40 on-demand.
cost-ops: acknowledged — will run pricing scenarios and return numbers by EOD Friday. :money_with_wings: 
serena: also put a monitoring alert to detect cross-AZ packet loss >0.5% — that should guard against network-induced latency cascades.
maya: perfect. filing follow-up thread for the simulation output. :thumbsup:
